record.original_question: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta, must its L(2,1)-labeling number satisfy lambda_{2,1}(G) <= Delta^2?

evidence.quote: L(2, 1)-Labeling Conjecture ([86]). Every graph G has λ2,1(G) 6 ∆2.
If graph G has maximum degree ∆, then λ2,1(G) 6 ∆2. This is the L(2, 1)-Labeling Conjecture, due to Griggs and Yeh. It has been proved for ∆ sufficiently large; see Theorem 41.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. An $L(2,1)$-labeling of $G$ is a function $f:V\to\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ such that:
- $|f(u)-f(v)|\ge 2$ whenever $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$, and
- $|f(u)-f(v)|\ge 1$ whenever $u$ and $v$ are at distance exactly $2$ in $G$.

The $L(2,1)$-labeling number $\lambda_{2,1}(G)$ is defined as the minimum over all $L(2,1)$-labelings $f$ of $G$ of $\max_{v\in V} f(v)$.

Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta=\Delta(G)\ge 2$,
$$\lambda_{2,1}(G)\le \Delta^2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture of Griggs and Yeh (1992) was settled by Havet, Reed, and Sereni for graphs whose maximum degree Δ exceeds a (very large) constant Δ₀, and it is known for many specific graph classes (chordal, outerplanar, certain Hamming and Petersen graphs, etc.). However, in full generality (all Δ ≥ 2) it remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Griggs and Yeh's Conjecture and L(p,1)-labelings
status_evidence.snippet: For any positive integer p there exists a constant Δ_p such that every graph with maximum degree Δ ≥ Δ_p has an L(p,1)-labeling with span at most Δ².
status_evidence.claim: Havet, Reed and Sereni proved the conjecture for sufficiently large Δ.

status_evidence.title: A proof of a version of Griggs and Yeh's conjecture for L(2,1)-labeling of iterated Mycielskians
status_evidence.snippet: Griggs and Yeh's conjecture ... remains unsolved in general; verified for several graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture remains open while many partial cases are confirmed.
